before.title: NCC morning presentation: AION C IDE and Software Developer Package
before.description: On the morning of 6 June 1978 at NCC in Anaheim, AION and Logix present the Aurelia development environment and Software Developer Package. The presentation explains platform and peripheral interfaces, edits and builds an application, links an assembly library, debugs a RAM application and demonstrates TUI forms and tested text/bitmap presentation. It reports measured resource use and distinguishes SDK helpers from ROM services.

inputs.description: The Aurelia C IDE and Developer Package supply the tools and documented interfaces used in the presentation.

outcomes.description: Developers see the Aurelia editing, compilation, library, debugging and TUI workflow with its measured resource limits and supported interface boundaries.
Full-session recordings and production masters of the developer presentation and questions are supplied for subsequent cleared editing and redistribution.

change.title: Reserve agreement_id for signing or contractual acceptance events
change.reason: Apply the author’s rule to every agreement: retain agreement_id only at an evidenced signing, formalisation or contractual acceptance event. Remove it from operational/cooperation events, acquisition closing, the Academy launch, implementation processes and the unsigned Apple–Peachtree negotiation. The October Logix share-transfer event records fulfilment of earlier commitments rather than a supported signing event, so its agreement_id is also removed without inventing another event. Retain all agreements, clauses, obligations, narrative relationships and prerequisite links. Correct the BPI cooperation outcome’s stale July 17 training date to the already approved June 16 Academy launch. The current compatibility schemas continue to read old records until approval.

before.title: AIONix exploratory and formal development
before.description: Develop AIONix from the exploratory architecture and portability milestone on 1 February 1978 through completion of this development phase on 20 February 1980, under the separately agreed ownership and later non-ERA porting rights. Commercial release with Artemis follows on 19 May 1980.

outcomes.description: The AIONix development phase is complete for handover to later Artemis integration and launch preparation; this outcome does not move commercial availability before 19 May 1980.

steps.description: AION Software and DRI began architecture, C portability and ERA operating-system work in February 1978.
Move the AIONix department from London to Logix offices near DRI headquarters on 24 February 1978. Letwin remains in London; a separate lead manages the relocated team.
Milestone during this process: AIONix development programme and ownership formalised.
Following the September agreement, the teams developed the ERA operating system while maintaining CP/M and the Aurelia release line.
Complete the October Logix transfer: Kildall and Comstock receive 10% each, and the CFO and Paterson 5% each. The promised interests are fulfilled once.
Prepare confidential next-generation system software, application migration and C tools for Artemis without public disclosure before NCC 1980.
Complete this phase of AIONix development by 20 February 1980 and hand the work over for subsequent platform integration and commercial launch preparation. Ongoing maintenance continues separately.

before.title: Autodesk funded development and acceptance
before.description: Autodesk funded development and acceptance Deliver AutoCAD 1.0 for Artemis/AIONix for the joint November 1982 COMDEX presentation; November release-quality build is the commitment, with commercial shipment subject to acceptance rather than automatically deferred to December.

inputs.description: The founders held an organising meeting on 30 January 1982. It provides the date basis and preparatory context for the agreement signed on 31 January, which starts this funded development programme. The source does not identify the meeting attendees.
Native AIONix/ERA build with reliable floating-point geometry and typed coordinate entry
Dual-display driver with colour command/status screen and 800x600 drawing canvas; independent palettes and explicit input focus
Explicit CAD mouse integration; standard TUI mouse support alone is insufficient
Drawing load/save and DXF exchange tests against the other supported AutoCAD builds
Supported pen-plotter output and physical drawing verification
Measured RAM, storage, redraw and stability requirements on the qualified configuration; backup/restore and reproducible release build
Feature baseline agreed with Autodesk; no automatic import of later AutoCAD dimensioning, object-snap or 3D features

team environment / workstations: Supply an Artemis PRO with 1 MiB RAM, local storage and available display to each assigned developer, plus shared build/test and spare machines as the agreed staffing plan requires. No invented fixed team size.

team environment / software: Install the entire AION Development System — Team Edition: C Development Environment 2, ERA compiler/linker/debugger and validated floating-point math library; source repository, branches/reviews, tasks, collaboration, reproducible builds, release labels and target testing.

team environment / network: Supply network adapters, hub, cabling, configured accounts and project permissions, and dedicated Artemis PRO server capacity. Scale sponsored server/license deployments to the whole team within qualified concurrency; the retail four-session entitlement is not silently unlimited.

team environment / storage: The standard 5 MB disk is inadequate as a presumed whole-team repository/build archive. Fund and qualify larger storage, additional volumes/servers, independent backup media, restore tests and off-machine source archives; capacities follow measured source/build/history budgets.

team environment / support: Fund dedicated Autodesk engineering time, AION compiler/runtime and integration specialists, installation, training, documentation, replacement hardware, plotter access and on-site support through release. Retail onboarding/support-hour caps do not limit this separately sponsored agreement.

team environment / early graphics: January work uses available Artemis PRO displays and a stable software implementation of the graphics API. Supply 64 KiB/Color Pro engineering samples and mouse prototypes when qualified; do not make January work depend on the June professional hardware.

team environment / professional handover: Around June 1982 deliver the 128 KiB professional card and Logix Mono Pro 17 to the development and QA team, alongside the 64 KiB colour card/Color Pro 14 and mouse. This supersedes the earlier proposed January 17-inch prototype handover.

funding: Adam commits to supplying the staffing, equipment, licences and integration resources required by the agreed delivery plan. No arbitrary dollar ceiling or fabricated cost estimate; procurement and staffing are reviewed against the November objective.

outcomes.description: Deliver AutoCAD 1.0 for Artemis/AIONix for the joint November 1982 COMDEX presentation; November release-quality build is the commitment, with commercial shipment subject to acceptance rather than automatically deferred to December.

Qualify the professional display interfaces required by the November CAD configuration, including inherited modes, palette sequencing and five-sprite compatibility. Preserve the separate June development handover; CAD development does not create the underlying graphics technology.

steps.description: Deliver AutoCAD 1.0 for Artemis/AIONix for the joint November 1982 COMDEX presentation; November release-quality build is the commitment, with commercial shipment subject to acceptance rather than automatically deferred to December.
Meet programme acceptance gates; commercial shipment remains conditional on acceptance.

After incorporation on 26 April 1982, Autodesk adopts the founders' development arrangement, confirms source/porting rights and non-exclusive licensing, and reviews the compiler, recovery and graphics-driver milestones.
Milestone during this process: Professional 800x600 hardware becomes available to Autodesk.
Milestone during this process: AutoCAD Artemis beta and professional workflow qualification.

before.title: BPI development and distribution cooperation
before.description: BPI and Adam implement operational cooperation under the consolidated BPI agreement: independent BPI management, brand, application ownership, licences and specialist support; AION engineering assistance and Logix distribution/training. This cooperation implements the accepted $150,000 investment agreement for Adam’s 33% fully diluted interest, including AION’s C/TUI redevelopment work and future-platform cooperation. Date selected for the alternative scenario. The cooperation also provides for later launch qualification, BPI-authorised Academy training and direct sales, with BPI retaining its software, independent licensing and specialist support.

inputs.description: BPI's accepted 15 February investment and C/TUI redevelopment agreement establishes the obligations implemented by this operational cooperation.

The cooperation supports a later programme of BPI-authorised courses and direct sales starting on 17 July 1978, after the NCC premiere. This start is separate from the Academy's March establishment and June 5 five-city public announcement.

before.title: Official Logix Computer Academy launch, including BPI training and distribution
before.description: On 16 June 1978, Logix Computer Academy officially launches its public training programme, including Aurelia Fundamentals and BPI-authorised offerings. Academy begins BPI-authorised practical courses and direct distribution alongside BPI dealer qualification, accountant demonstration access, permission-based case studies and defined setup assistance. Each initial Academy centre has access to a BPI specialist. Dealers handle first-line installation enquiries, BPI handles software defects and specialist support, and Logix supports hardware. Training, setup services and software licences remain separate offerings.

participant.role: authorised training and direct distribution provider

inputs.description: The BPI application launch establishes the product offering for subsequent authorised training, direct distribution and dealer demonstrations.
Separately licensed BPI applications are the subject of the authorised courses, direct distribution and dealer demonstrations. They remain BPI offerings rather than newly created Academy software.
The Academy company and its preparation of the initial five-city programme provide the organisation and facilities basis for the public launch.

outcomes.description: The Academy publicly launches hands-on Aurelia training, configuration advice and direct ordering; customer-site delivery remains an option and immediate collection depends on stock.

Authorised BPI training, direct sales and the qualified dealer programme are operating with defined support responsibilities and access to BPI specialists. The programme also establishes follow-up plans for year-end preparation, module-upgrade demonstrations and expansion based on verified customer results; this does not assert completion of those later activities.

before.title: Model II software and interface cooperation
before.description: Develop and qualify native-display Model II CP/M, Abacus and the separately supported FlexiBUS option, concluding with the Tandy-led customer release on 15 October 1979. Tandy retains its hardware platform, sales and promotion; DRI and AION retain their respective software responsibilities.

inputs.description: The cooperation must preserve the Model II native hardware architecture and satisfy its internal bus and host-interface constraints.

outcomes.description: Deliver the Model II CP/M and Abacus implementations and the qualified Model-II-specific FlexiBUS option while retaining Tandy’s existing host architecture. These outputs do not create the Model II computer or the FlexiBUS standard.

steps.description: Sign the Model II CP/M, FlexiBUS and Abacus cooperation agreement.
Agree the Model II compatibility design baseline and responsibilities.
Review prototype CP/M boot, native TUI, Abacus interchange, memory limits and the Model-II-specific FlexiBUS interface.
Announce the planned supported Model II CP/M, FlexiBUS and Abacus offering, distinguishing planned availability from completed sales.
Demonstrate the qualified Model II prototype at NCC while distinguishing demonstration from autumn customer release.
Conclude the cooperation with the supported customer release through the Tandy-led Model II campaign, after the required software and interface qualification.
Coordinate the marketing campaign: Tandy Model II supported configuration launch.
